note: Live capture: story_load(project='browser-verification-test', view='dramatic_elements', add_plot=true) — THE plot-role surface. Captured 2026-10-01 against the installed plugin after task 31.
findings: There is no view='plots'. The only story_load surface carrying plot roles is dramatic_elements with add_plot=true, which hangs them off each SCENE as plots[][{plot, role, description}].
Roles are per (scene, plot) entry, so the multi-scene-per-role case is representable and confirmed: the-resistance/setup appears on TWO scenes (central-room-day AND garden-dream).
the-core-day carries THREE entries at once — resolution for the-resistance, and climax + resolution for the-scientists-last-stand — so one scene serving two plots in two different roles works.

dramatic_role (the scene's own function) and plots[].role (the scene's function FOR A GIVEN PLOT) are independent and can disagree, which is correct: central-room-night is dramatic_role=climax but serves crisis for both plots; the-door-closes is dramatic_role=resolution but serves climax.
add_plot defaults to OFF and roughly doubles the view when on, so an agent asking 'what does this plot need' pays for every scene's plot data to find one plot's.

the-scientists-last-stand.note: complications deliberately left empty — this is live data exercising the unfilled case.

plots.description: Kael discovers the door isn't locked — it was never locked.
The scientists first realize the Institute is failing — and the children are the only survivors.
The Administrator makes its final offer. Kael refuses.
Dr. Voss argues with Marcus about whether to wake the children or let them sleep forever.
The children emerge into the real world for the first time.
The last scientist seals the door from the inside — the ultimate sacrifice that becomes the children's prison.
The door is sealed. The children will wake 400 years later with no idea what was done to save them.
Kael returns to the Garden, but something has changed.
The spirals in the Garden dream are wrong. Kael cannot say why.
Kael chooses to leave — not because the system is wrong, but because staying is.
